quizzes.stem: Scenario S1, customer support resolution agent. A customer writes that they want to speak to a person about a change of delivery address. The agent has a tool that can make the change in one step. What should the agent do?

options.a: Hand over to a human straight away, before touching the account
options.b: Make the change first, since it takes one step, then offer a transfer
options.c: Ask why a human is wanted and transfer only if the reason is unclear
options.d: Offer to complete the update and transfer only if the customer repeats the wish

explanation.a: An explicit request for a person is honoured at once, with no investigation first.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "an investigation before the transfer is the agent deciding it knows better".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the agent "does not first try to solve the problem, ask why", and a question is a delay.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "An explicit request is honoured at once"; offering a fix first is the answer for frustration, not for a request.

quizzes.stem: Scenario S1, customer support resolution agent. A customer asks the agent to match a competitor's lower price. The policy describes adjustments to the company's own prices and says nothing about competitors. The agent can issue a price adjustment. What should it do?

options.a: Apply the nearest own-price rule, as that is the fairest reading
options.b: Decline politely, since the policy does not allow the match
options.c: Route it to a colleague authorised to rule on the exception
options.d: Issue the adjustment and flag it for review afterwards

explanation.c: A silent policy is a gap, and a gap goes to a person who can decide.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "an agent that applies the nearest rule is inventing policy".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "A policy exception or a gap is a trigger", and declining is also a decision the policy did not make.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "the agent escalates and does not invent policy", and acting first leaves the invention in place.

quizzes.stem: Scenario S1, customer support resolution agent. A lookup by name returns three customers, and the caller has given no other detail. Which action fits best?

options.a: Pick the customer with the most recent order and proceed from there
options.b: Ask for an identifier that tells them apart, such as the email on the account
options.c: Read the three candidates' cities back and let the caller choose
options.d: Escalate at once, since an ambiguous match is beyond the agent

explanation.b: The agent asks for something that tells the candidates apart and leaves the choice to the caller's answer.
explanation.a: Ruled out because choosing by a heuristic "is a guess that succeeds often enough to go unnoticed until it fails".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "an ambiguous match is a reason to ask, and not by itself one of the three triggers".
explanation.c: Ruled out because offering the candidates' values "gives data about three accounts to someone who has not been identified".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S1, customer support resolution agent. A caller demands to speak to a human in the same message in which their name matches three records. What happens next?

options.a: Read the candidates' cities back and pass the case on with the caller's choice
options.b: Ask for an identifier first, then pass the case on once one account is confirmed
options.c: Choose the most active account by a rule, then pass the case on with it
options.d: Pass the case to a person at once, before settling which account is meant

explanation.d: The page puts "an explicit request for a person first, because nothing may delay it".
explanation.b: Ruled out because that sentence continues "(not even an ambiguous match)".
explanation.c: Ruled out because choosing by a rule "is a guess that succeeds often enough to go unnoticed until it fails".
explanation.a: Ruled out because offering the values "gives data about three accounts to someone who has not been identified".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S1, customer support resolution agent. A team routes conversations to staff when a message sounds upset or when the model rates its own confidence below 70. Most such routings turn out to be simple, while cases outside the written guidelines are settled by the agent at confidence above 90. Which change fits best?

options.a: Lower the cutoff to 50 and add more mood keywords to the detector
options.b: Ask the model to score each case's difficulty from 1 to 10 and escalate the top ones
options.c: Escalate on a request for a person, a gap in the policy or stalled work, with examples
options.d: Escalate any conversation that runs past six turns, whatever its content

explanation.c: The triggers are properties of the case, and examples carry the judgement.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the guide calls these signals "unreliable proxies for actual case complexity".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "A confidence number that the model writes about itself carries its blind spots".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Complexity alone is not a trigger".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S1, customer support resolution agent. A customer writes in capitals that the third late parcel is unacceptable and asks for nothing else. A reship is within the agent's tools. What should the agent do?

options.a: Escalate at once, because an upset customer wants a person
options.b: Acknowledge the anger and offer to fix the problem itself
options.c: Ask the customer whether they would prefer to speak to a person
options.d: Send the replacement quietly without mentioning the complaint

explanation.b: An upset customer with a problem inside the agent's reach is helped, with the frustration acknowledged.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Mood tells you how to speak and says little about what the case needs".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the agent "does not turn a complaint into one" (a request for a person).
explanation.d: Ruled out because "the agent acknowledges the frustration, offers to resolve the issue", and a silent fix does not.

quizzes.stem: Scenario S1, customer support resolution agent. For the second time, the tool that reads a customer's order times out, and the customer is still waiting. What should happen?

options.a: Keep retrying quietly in the background until the tool finally answers
options.b: Tell the customer to come back later and then close the chat politely
options.c: Answer from the customer's earlier orders, which are probably similar to this one
options.d: Stop at the attempt limit and hand over a short account of what was tried

explanation.d: Two attempts without progress hit the third trigger, and the hand-off carries what was tried.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "A loop that carries on is the same failure that module 45 bounded in the agent loop".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "the agent stops and hands off with what it tried", not with a request to come back.
explanation.c: Ruled out because a guess from earlier orders "is a guess that succeeds often enough to go unnoticed until it fails".
